summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with palpitations and worsening shortness of breath following a recent hospitalization for multifocal pneumonia and COPD exacerbation. He was found to have atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular rate, decompensated systolic heart failure, and signs of recurrent pulmonary infiltrate. Treatment included rate control with metoprolol, diuresis for fluid overload, and completion of antibiotic therapy. His COPD was managed with steroids and bronchodilators, and he was transitioned from Advair to fluticasone to reduce cardiac stimulation. His kidney function improved with hydration. He received methadone for opioid withdrawal and expressed strong motivation to pursue recovery. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up arranged for cardiology, pulmonary, and addiction services.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
